name: Mesosiderite Type A1
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class A and textural (metamorphic) grade 1: basaltic, plagioclase-rich silicates (>25 vol% modal plagioclase, <65 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene); matrix of abundant fine-grained silicates (many <10 um) with pronounced cataclastic texture, angular fragments at all sizes, and little or no inversion of pigeonite to orthopyroxene.
source: Powell (1971); Floran (1978); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Zachen et al. (2025); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: 7 classified in MetBull, incl. 3 of the 7 observed mesosiderite falls: Barea (1842), Dyarrl Island (1933), Patwar (1935); also Vaca Muerta (3.83 t, largest mesosiderite), Crab Orchard, Mount Padbury; Acfer 265 and QUE 86900 assigned A1 by Zachen et al. (2025).

name: Mesosiderite Type A2
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class A and textural (metamorphic) grade 2: basaltic, plagioclase-rich silicates (>25 vol% modal plagioclase, <65 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene); matrix grains mostly >10 um, cataclastic angularity limited to larger fragments, and minor pigeonite partially inverted to orthopyroxene.
source: Powell (1971); Floran (1978); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: 6 classified in MetBull: Clover Springs, NWA 1242, NWA 2815, NWA 10882, NWA 15114, NWA 15548; NWA 14599 is transitional A2/3.

name: Mesosiderite Type A3
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class A and textural (metamorphic) grade 3: basaltic, plagioclase-rich silicates (>25 vol% modal plagioclase, <65 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene); recrystallized matrix with most grains >100 um, no microscopic cataclastic angularity (brecciation evident only macroscopically), and extensive pigeonite-to-orthopyroxene inversion.
source: Powell (1971); Floran (1978); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: Most populous subgroup: 22 classified in MetBull, incl. the Lowicz fall (1935, Poland); Emery, Morristown, NWA 8402 (23.85 kg); the Estherville fall (1879, 320 kg) is transitional A3/4.

name: Mesosiderite Type A4
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class A and textural grade 4: basaltic, plagioclase-rich silicates (>25 vol% modal plagioclase, <65 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene); igneous-textured melt matrix (subophitic to plagioclase-poikilitic) without cataclastic texture, the igneous grade added by Hewins (1984).
source: Powell (1971); Floran (1978); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Zachen et al. (2025); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: 6 classified in MetBull: Hainholz, Pinnaroo, Simondium, NWA 8741 (22.3 kg), NWA 14571, NWA 17025; MAC 88102 assigned A4 by Zachen et al. (2025).

name: Mesosiderite Type B1
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class B and textural (metamorphic) grade 1: ultramafic, orthopyroxene-rich silicates (5-25 vol% modal plagioclase, 65-85 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene); matrix of abundant fine-grained silicates (many <10 um) with pronounced cataclastic texture, angular fragments at all sizes, and little or no inversion of pigeonite to orthopyroxene.
source: Powell (1971); Floran (1978); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: 4 classified in MetBull: Chinguetti (Mauritania, 1920), ALH A77219, ALH A81059, ALH A81098; Antarctic members assigned by Hewins (1988).

name: Mesosiderite Type B2
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class B and textural (metamorphic) grade 2: ultramafic, orthopyroxene-rich silicates (5-25 vol% modal plagioclase, 65-85 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene); matrix grains mostly >10 um, cataclastic angularity limited to larger fragments, and minor pigeonite partially inverted to orthopyroxene.
source: Powell (1971); Floran (1978); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: 11 classified in MetBull, incl. the Veramin fall (1880, Iran, 54 kg); NWA 15346 (67.5 kg), NWA 1979 (5.12 kg), NWA 4049, Catalina 392, Catalina 399; NWA 13532 is transitional B2/3.

name: Mesosiderite Type B3
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class B and textural (metamorphic) grade 3: ultramafic, orthopyroxene-rich silicates (5-25 vol% modal plagioclase, 65-85 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene); recrystallized matrix with most grains >100 um, no microscopic cataclastic angularity (brecciation evident only macroscopically), and extensive pigeonite-to-orthopyroxene inversion.
source: Powell (1971); Floran (1978); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Zachen et al. (2025); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: Rarest occupied cell: 1 classified in MetBull (NWA 8742); Lamont, long listed as B3, was reclassified as B4 (tentatively B3/4) by Zachen et al. (2025).

name: Mesosiderite Type B4
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class B and textural grade 4: ultramafic, orthopyroxene-rich silicates (5-25 vol% modal plagioclase, 65-85 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene); igneous-textured melt matrix (subophitic to plagioclase-poikilitic) without cataclastic texture, the igneous grade added by Hewins (1984).
source: Powell (1971); Floran (1978); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Zachen et al. (2025); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: 4 classified in MetBull: Bondoc (888.6 kg, the most massive subgrouped mesosiderite), Budulan (100 kg), Mincy (89.4 kg), Timbuktu; Lamont (38.69 kg) added as B4 (or B3/4) by Zachen et al. (2025).

name: Mesosiderite Type C1
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class C and textural (metamorphic) grade 1: orthopyroxenite-dominated, plagioclase-poor silicates (<5 vol% modal plagioclase, >85 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene), the most magnesian mesosiderite class; matrix of abundant fine-grained silicates (many <10 um) with pronounced cataclastic texture, angular fragments at all sizes, and little or no inversion of pigeonite to orthopyroxene.
source: Powell (1971); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: No classified members in MetBull to date; cell defined by the scheme but so far unoccupied. 9 stones carry class C without a grade (e.g. Youxi, 218 kg; NWA 1951, 17 kg; NWA 1827 pairing group).

name: Mesosiderite Type C2
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class C and textural (metamorphic) grade 2: orthopyroxenite-dominated, plagioclase-poor silicates (<5 vol% modal plagioclase, >85 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene), the most magnesian mesosiderite class; matrix grains mostly >10 um, cataclastic angularity limited to larger fragments, and minor pigeonite partially inverted to orthopyroxene.
source: Powell (1971); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: 5 classified in MetBull: Jiddat al Harasis 203 (46.2 kg), Jiddat al Harasis 845, NWA 7909, NWA 8234, Ramlat as Sahmah 384 (5.03 kg) - all hot-desert finds.

name: Mesosiderite Type C3
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class C and textural (metamorphic) grade 3: orthopyroxenite-dominated, plagioclase-poor silicates (<5 vol% modal plagioclase, >85 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene), the most magnesian mesosiderite class; recrystallized matrix with most grains >100 um, no microscopic cataclastic angularity (brecciation evident only macroscopically), and extensive pigeonite-to-orthopyroxene inversion.
source: Powell (1971); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: 2 classified in MetBull: NWA 12566 (2.9 kg), San Juan 116 (447 g, Atacama).

name: Mesosiderite Type C4
description: Mesosiderite of mineralogical class C and textural grade 4: orthopyroxenite-dominated, plagioclase-poor silicates (<5 vol% modal plagioclase, >85 vol% Ca-poor pyroxene), the most magnesian mesosiderite class; igneous-textured melt matrix (subophitic to plagioclase-poikilitic) without cataclastic texture, the igneous grade added by Hewins (1984).
source: Powell (1971); Hewins (1984); Mittlefehldt et al. (1998); Hutchison (2004); Meteoritical Bulletin Database (accessed 2026-09-11)
notes: No classified members in MetBull to date; cell defined by the scheme but so far unoccupied. Anomalous magnesian mesosiderites (e.g. RKP A79015, Chaunskij) are classified Mesosiderite-an rather than C4.
